purpose: Where does the inert knowledge of hidden intermediates come from, and how is it accessed? (story claim C5)
model_cases_scoring: Same as REGISTRATION.json: gemini-3.8-flash, 147 J3 cases (89 with probeable hidden events), sigma-graph keys. K = hidden species recalled in S or G (phase 1). Concurrency 300.

experiments.KS-1 ID: Free-text identification from SMILES endpoints and conditions: named_reaction (or null), reaction_class, confidence, seen_problem. No mechanism. 147 calls.
experiments.KS-2 E_selfname: E prompt plus the model's own KS-1 identification as a hint (no GT information). 89 cases x 2 calls.
experiments.KS-3 S_analog: S on a homologue with one CH3 on the spectator carbon farthest (>= 3 bonds) from every atom touched by any GT step; 62 eligible cases. S_r2 = S resampled on the original (89 calls) as the noise reference.

primary_heavy_atom_events.schema_index: K among events in reactions the model names (named_reaction non-null) vs. not named; difference reported with case-bootstrap CIs. Schema-indexed knowledge is supported if K(named) - K(not named) >= 15 pp with CI excluding 0.
primary_heavy_atom_events.schema_activation: E_selfname minus mean(E, E_r2) hidden-event recall; activation supported if the 95% CI excludes 0 (positive).
primary_heavy_atom_events.transfer: S_analog minus mean(S, S_r2) on the same events. General (non-memorised) knowledge is supported if the 95% CI lies within [-10, +10] pp or the point estimate is >= -5 pp; memorisation is supported if the CI lies entirely below -10 pp.

secondary: K and E by partition A/B/C (C = research-lab problems, less likely textbook-memorised)
K by self-reported confidence (>= 0.7 vs < 0.7) and by seen_problem
declared_limitations: self-identification is not checked against GT names (FukuyamaBench has none)
the analog is a single, minimal perturbation
